title: Predict the guarded program
idea: Read small guarded programs and predict the output for both the normal case and the edge case. Pure thinking.

exercises.explanation: count is 0, so the guard fires: No average. The division it protects is safely skipped.
count is 5, so count == 0 is False; the normal branch runs: Has average.
items is 0, so the guard prints Empty rather than the awkward number 0.
items is 7, so the else prints the value 7.
-1 < 0 is True, so the guard catches the impossible age: Invalid.
0 < 0 is False, so the else runs: OK. Note zero age is not negative, so it passes this guard.

exercises.prompt: In a guarded if/else, exactly one branch runs - either the guard or the normal case.
exercises.explanation: Right. Just like any if/else, one path always runs and only one.
people is 0, so the guard prints Nobody here and the division is skipped - no crash.
stock is 3, so stock == 0 is False; the normal branch runs: Available.

exercises.prompt: Across all these, what makes a guard valuable?
options: It gives a sensible answer for the edge case instead of a crash or nonsense
It removes the need for comparisons
exercises.explanation: A guard turns a dangerous or nonsensical edge case into a clear, deliberate answer. That is the whole point.
